content.text:
Fixed: picking a To date in the same quarter as From no longer flips the range. The `reportRanges` tests pass, including the new one. I didn't try it in the running app.

**Cause:** `validateEnd` in `reportRanges.ts` compared the stored From date (`'2026-07-01'`) with the raw To pick (`'2026-07'`). As strings, the longer one sorts later, so the code treated the range as reversed. It then replaced From with the four-quarter fallback.

**Fix:** it now compares From against the normalized end of the picked quarter (`'2026-09-30'`). The same string comparison existed for Monthly and Yearly, so it should also have affected a To in the same month or year as From. The change covers those too.

**Test:** I added a case to `reportRanges.test.ts` for a To in the same quarter as From. It covers the first and last month of the quarter.

Vitest needed Node 22 here. The default shell is on Node 18, so I used the nvm 22.20.0 install.

message.content: ah nice, so it was comparing the full From date against the short period key, which sorts wrong. comparing real computed dates is the right call. does the fallback still give four whole quarters when one end actually passes the other?

content.text:
Yes. The fallback still gives four whole quarters when one end passes the other, and the existing tests cover it.

- **To moved before From:** the fallback sets From to the first day of the quarter nine months before the picked quarter. With From at `2016-07-01` and To picked as `2016-01`, the result is `2015-04-01` to `2016-03-31`, which is four whole quarters. The old assertions still pass because the reversed case compares as reversed under the new check too (`2016-07-01` is after `2016-03-31`).
- **From moved after To:** I didn't touch `validateStart`. It compares the stored end date (a full date) with the short From pick, and the old bug doesn't happen there. For example, an end of `2015-09-30` against a From of `2015-07` isn't flagged as reversed. A From of `2015-10` is flagged, and falls back to `2015-10-01` through `2016-09-30`.

The one case that isn't a fallback is a To in the same quarter as From. It keeps From and gives one whole quarter, such as `2015-07-01` to `2015-09-30`.

message.content: nice, the stash check was a good call. one thing, when To is a year like '2015', how does it get to the end date? is that going through the month helpers or its own string math?

content.text:
Its own string math. In `validateEnd`, the Yearly case is:

```ts
case 'Yearly':
  dateEnd = end + '-12-31';
  subDays = 1095;
```

So a To of `'2015'` becomes `'2015-12-31'` by appending. It doesn't go through `getMonthEnd` or any other month helper. That works because every year ends on Dec 31, so there's no month length or leap-year logic to get wrong. `validateStart` does the same thing, with `start + '-01-01'`.

Monthly and Quarterly do use the month helpers. Monthly calls `getMonthEnd(end + '-01')`, and Quarterly calls `getMonthEnd(getQuarterEnd(end) + '-01')`.

This relies on To being a bare four-digit year when the interval is Yearly. The To dropdown passes keys in that shape. If a full date such as `'2015-12-31'` ever reached that branch, you'd get `'2015-12-31-12-31'`. I haven't checked whether any saved-report path can produce that. I can check if you want.

**Saved reports can't hand that branch a full date.** I traced it from the code but didn't run it against a saved report.

- **Only caller:** `validateStart` and `validateEnd` are called in one place, the From/To `Select` `onChange` handlers in `ReportSidebar.tsx`. Loading a saved report goes through `setReportData` in `CustomReport.tsx`, which sets the dates directly and never calls the validators.
- **What To can be:** the `newValue` comes from the `allIntervals` options, which `onSetAllIntervals` builds from the range helpers. For Yearly that's `yearRangeInclusive`, whose values are formatted `yyyy`. Yearly To can only be a bare four-digit year.
- **Stale To after a switch:** if you switch the interval to Yearly while a full-date `endDate` is stored, nothing calls `validateEnd` with that value. It only runs when you pick a new To, and then the value is a fresh `yyyy` key.

The other input, `start`, does come from stored state and can be in any shape, including from a saved report. It is only used in the `start > dateEnd` comparison, so a mismatched shape would give a wrong comparison, not a malformed date. I didn't check how switching the interval resets the stored dates.

**Casts:** the quarterly commit added no new `as` casts to production code.

- **Existing cast, extended:** in `CustomReport.tsx`, the `fromDate` string cast already existed. I added `'quarterFromDate'` to its union, so the cast is wider, not new.
- **New casts in a test file:** the other three are in `fetchSpreadsheetQueryData.test.ts`. Two are `as CategoryEntity[]` and `as CategoryGroupEntity[]` on fixtures. The third is `as unknown as typeof send` on a mock, which is the one worth a second look.

The `fromDate` cast is the only one that could hide a real mistake. It builds a method name by string concatenation, so a typo in an interval name wouldn't be a type error. I can replace it with a lookup map if you'd like.
